title: The Gift of Many Teachers
author: Dave Stuart Jr.
summary: Stuart describes a message he repeats often to his students: that they have far more teachers available to them than just the adult standing at the front of the room. He counts through the full roster - themselves as the primary agent of their own learning, the classroom teacher as the discipline expert, in-person support staff like paraprofessionals and ESL specialists, YouTube educators he intentionally weaves into lessons, and the texts students read. He includes a practical aside about the importance of pausing video content to let students discuss and process, treating outside media as "guest teachers" rather than passive filler. The larger aim is to give students a mindset - "I can learn all the time, I can learn anything, from anyone" - that Stuart considers essential to a flourishing life, delivered through deliberate repetition rather than a single announcement.
points: Positions the student as their own first and last teacher, since no one else can access what they're thinking or unsure about - the reason open-source courseware alone hasn't produced a "society of geniuses."
Treats curated YouTube educators as "guest teachers" who can be paused mid-video for discussion, warning that skipping the pause step is a common, costly teacher oversight.
Frames the message's effectiveness as dependent on deliberate repetition, not a single announcement - students "need us to be very repetitive on this front."
Distills the payoff into a portable, one-line mindset for students: "I can learn all the time. I can learn anything, from anyone."
quotes: First and last, they have themselves. No one else in the world is more able to see the things they're thinking, the things they're wondering, the things they're confident or unsure about.
The journey of education is one that must be walked with one's own two feet. This is why open sourced education projects - e.g., MIT's Open Courseware - have not resulted in a society of geniuses.
I've made that my business and my craft, to find ways that work best for advancing a learner toward mastery and to make those ways accessible and ubiquitous in my classroom.
They become guest teachers whom I can pause at any time so that we might discuss or take notes or clear up confusions.
What we're doing as we point their eyes toward the many teachers they have is gaining them access to a view of the world that is so helpful for a flourishing life.
Wow. I can learn all the time. I can learn anything, from anyone.
